articles.title: Is Hemiepiphysiodesis Enough? Evaluating Growth Modulation in Juvenile Hallux Valgus.
articles.authors: Bozorgmehr CK, Tang N, Abbas Y, Hosseinzadeh P
articles.sample_size: 20 feet in 13 children, mean age 10 years
articles.outcomes: Radiographic correction of hallux valgus angle and intermetatarsal angle; need for further surgery; residual deformity
articles.take_home: Hemiepiphysiodesis, a minimally invasive growth-modulation procedure, produces modest improvements in bunion measurements but leaves significant deformity in 80% of cases, with about one-third of patients needing additional corrective surgery within 6 years. It may delay the need for traditional surgery but is unlikely to prevent it entirely.

articles.title: Spinal Fusion in Prader-Willi Syndrome: Early Radiographic Outcomes and Complications With a Subset Analysis of Two-year Follow-up in a Multicenter Cohort.
articles.authors: Lobato AG, Andras L, Vaughan M, Ramo BA, McQuerry JL, Huser AJ, et al.
articles.population: Children with Prader-Willi syndrome undergoing spinal fusion
articles.outcomes: Spinal curve correction, complications, unplanned return to operating room, pulmonary function and satisfaction scores
articles.take_home: Spinal fusion in children with Prader-Willi syndrome successfully corrects the spine curvature and maintains this improvement, but nearly 1 in 5 patients needed unplanned return surgery and over 1 in 5 experienced complications, particularly those with higher body weight.

articles.title: Diagnosis and Treatment of Concomitant Lateral Condyle and Medial Epicondyle Fractures With Elbow Dislocation in Children.
articles.authors: Lu Y, Xue C, Canavese F, Xu T, Wu X, Lin J, et al.
articles.population: Children with concomitant lateral condyle and medial epicondyle fractures with elbow dislocation
articles.outcomes: Carrying angle, range of motion, elbow performance score, fracture healing time, and complications
articles.take_home: This rare injury affecting both sides of the elbow joint was treated surgically in all 12 children, with all fractures healing within 4 to 8 weeks. Most children (92%) had excellent outcomes and none had poor results, suggesting that proper surgery based on how the injury occurred leads to favourable results.

articles.title: Patient-reported Outcomes Measurement Information System Score Analysis in Diagnosis and Treatment Evaluation of Pediatric Disc Herniation Patients: A Preliminary Study.
articles.authors: Boebel GG, Wright CE, Mohseni M, Agrawal RR, Chen L, Lambrechts MJ, et al.
articles.population: Children under 18 years old with diagnosed intervertebral disc herniation
articles.outcomes: PROMIS Pain Interference and Mobility scores at presentation and follow-up; comparison between non-operative and surgical treatment groups
articles.take_home: Children with disc herniation have significantly worse pain and mobility than average. Those having surgery start with worse symptoms but improve mobility faster than those treated without surgery, and both groups end up with similar final scores.

articles.title: Intramedullary Nailing Following Tibia Lengthening With External Fixator in Fibular Hemimelia Reduces the Risk of Fractures.
articles.authors: Shadi M, Janusz P, Kortus E, Tschurl J, Kotwicki T
articles.population: Children with fibular hemimelia undergoing tibial lengthening
articles.outcomes: Fracture rate, infection rate, and need for unplanned reoperations after external fixator removal
articles.take_home: Children who had a metal rod inserted into the tibia bone after lengthening treatment had no fractures, whereas 25% of children treated with a cast had fractures. Neither group developed infections when antibiotics were used after rod insertion.

articles.title: Reoperations After Soft Tissue Release for Spastic Hip Displacement: Which One Matters More-Migration Percentage, Acetabular Index, or Motor Function?
articles.authors: Uy ARS, Wang SY, Hsu CM, Kao HK, Chang CH
articles.population: Children with hip displacement due to cerebral palsy who underwent soft tissue release surgery
articles.outcomes: Need for further surgery within 5 years after initial soft tissue release; predictive factors included acetabular index, migration percentage, motor function level, and windswept deformity
articles.take_home: The shape of the hip socket (acetabular index) before surgery was a better predictor of whether children would need further operations than the degree of hip displacement alone. Surgeons should consider the hip socket shape alongside displacement measurements when deciding on treatment.

articles.title: International Delphi Consensus on the Diagnosis and Management of Septic Arthritis of the Hip in Prewalking Children.
articles.authors: Shah H, Belthur MV, Ranade A, Ganjwala D, Agarwal A, Monsell F, et al.
articles.population: Fellowship-trained paediatric orthopaedic surgeons from 12 countries
articles.sample_size: 45 surgeons invited; 35 completed round 1; 32 completed round 2
articles.outcomes: Consensus statements on diagnosis and management of septic arthritis of the hip in prewalking children, covering clinical signs, imaging, surgical approach, postoperative care and follow-up
articles.take_home: International experts agreed on key principles for treating hip infections in babies and young children, including looking for pain on movement as the main sign, using surgery as first-line treatment (not antibiotics alone), and following up for at least 2 years. However, some areas like the use of routine ultrasound still need further research.

articles.title: Trial of a Maternal Diet Rich in Eggs and Peanuts to Reduce Infant Allergy.
articles.authors: Palmer DJ, Campbell DE, Nanan R, Hsu PS, Jorgensen AM, O'Sullivan M, et al.
articles.population: Pregnant women whose unborn child had at least two biological family members with medically diagnosed allergic disease
articles.sample_size: 2137 pregnant women (1070 high egg-peanut group, 1067 standard-diet group)
articles.outcomes: IgE-mediated egg or peanut allergy in infants at 1 year of age
articles.take_home: Eating high amounts of eggs and peanuts during pregnancy and breastfeeding did not reduce the risk of egg or peanut allergy in babies by age 1 compared with eating lower amounts of these foods. The rates of allergy were similar in both groups, at around 8 percent.

articles.title: Blinatumomab for Replacing Chemotherapy in Pediatric Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia.
articles.authors: Schrappe M, Locatelli F, Valsecchi MG, Zugmaier G, Vossen-Gajcy M, Stary J, et al.
articles.population: Children with newly diagnosed high-risk B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukaemia
articles.outcomes: 4-year event-free survival was 83.0% with blinatumomab versus 70.3% with chemotherapy. Fewer serious infections (23.9% vs 69.4%) and life-threatening adverse events (0.5% vs 4.7%) with blinatumomab, but more neurotoxic events (12.0% vs 3.2%).
articles.take_home: Children who received blinatumomab instead of chemotherapy had better survival rates at 4 years and experienced fewer serious infections and life-threatening side effects, although some developed nerve-related side effects more often. This suggests blinatumomab may be a safer alternative to traditional chemotherapy for this group of children.

articles.title: Utilizing Robotic-Assisted Navigation in Early Onset Scoliosis: Experience From a Multicenter Registry.
articles.authors: Williams CJ, Marsh IG, Sullivan ML, Hedequist D, Erickson MA, Hogue GD, et al.
articles.population: Children aged 9 years and younger with early onset scoliosis (idiopathic, neuromuscular, congenital, or syndromic)
articles.outcomes: Robotic screw placement success rate (97% of screws placed without difficulty or malposition), intraoperative complications (registration issues, calibration loss), postoperative complications including unplanned return to operating room, infection, and neurological events
articles.take_home: Robotic-assisted navigation successfully placed 97% of screws in children with early onset scoliosis with low rates of screw malposition, though technical challenges occurred in about one-third of patients. Overall, 16% of patients experienced postoperative complications, with 2 requiring unplanned return to surgery.

articles.title: Post-surgical Outcomes in Pediatric and Adolescent Patients With Osteogenesis Imperfecta Undergoing Knee Arthroscopy.
articles.authors: Allahverdian AT, Combs K, Weiss JM, Poon SC, Nguyen CV
articles.study_type: Retrospective case series across multiple centres
articles.population: Paediatric and adolescent patients with osteogenesis imperfecta
articles.outcomes: Postoperative complications, revision surgery rates, return to baseline activity, time to regain full range of motion
articles.take_home: Knee arthroscopy is safe for young people with osteogenesis imperfecta and most return to full activities within about 6 months, but complications and need for further surgery are more common than in other young people, so patients need to be prepared for this.

articles.title: Concomitant Open Reduction Does Not Improve Outcomes in Patients Undergoing Osseous Reconstruction for Severe Hip Dysplasia Secondary to Cerebral Palsy: A Radiographic and Clinical Comparative Analysis.
articles.authors: Dopke K, Campbell R, Talathi N, Bomar JD, Elias A, Thompson RM
articles.population: Children with cerebral palsy and severe hip subluxation or dislocation
articles.sample_size: 108 hips in 88 patients (30 with open reduction, 78 without)
articles.outcomes: Radiographic measurements (migration percentage), operative time, blood loss, medical complications, surgical complications, and need for further surgery
articles.take_home: Adding open reduction to hip reconstruction surgery in children with cerebral palsy caused longer operating times, more bleeding, and higher complication rates without improving the final hip position. The study suggests open reduction may not be necessary as part of this surgery.

articles.title: Surgical Outcome of Modified Woodward Procedure in Congenital Undescended Scapula.
articles.authors: Shahcheraghi GH, Javid M, Farsimadan M
articles.population: Children with Sprengel deformity (undescended scapula), some with associated congenital scoliosis
articles.sample_size: 27 shoulders in 25 patients, mean age 7.6 years
articles.outcomes: Improved shoulder function and appearance on clinical grading scales, shoulder movement increased by 34-39 degrees, Oxford Shoulder Score 42.5 out of 48, improved scapular position on X-rays
articles.take_home: Surgery to lower the elevated shoulder blade using the modified Woodward procedure significantly improved shoulder movement and function in children, with most patients satisfied and able to do most everyday activities. The operation worked well even in older children and those with additional spine curvature.

articles.title: Efficacy of antibiotic-loaded calcium sulphate pellets in the surgical management of chronic hematogenous osteomyelitis in children: a retrospective comparative study.
articles.authors: Thuppale VE, Mrudula K, Arikrishnan A, Reddy J, Gahukamble A, Palocaren T
articles.population: Children aged 16 years or under with chronic hematogenous osteomyelitis treated surgically
articles.sample_size: 55 children (55 limbs): 38 treated with debridement alone, 17 treated with debridement and antibiotic-loaded calcium sulphate pellets
articles.outcomes: Recurrence rates, healing rates, reoperation rates, and complication rates
articles.take_home: Children who received antibiotic-loaded calcium sulphate pellets alongside surgery had significantly lower rates of infection recurrence and complications, with better healing compared to surgery alone. This benefit was particularly noticeable in a specific type of bone lesion.

articles.title: Classification of Forearm Involvement in Multiple Hereditary Exostoses: Consensus from the CoULD Study Group.
articles.authors: Vuillermin C, Canizares MF, Miller PE, Wall LB, Steinman SE, Van Heest A
articles.study_type: Consensus-based classification development using Delphi methodology
articles.population: Patients with multiple hereditary exostoses and forearm deformities
articles.sample_size: 67 patients (101 radiographs) for reliability testing; 15 surgeons in Delphi process; 4 independent surgeons for validation
articles.outcomes: Reliability of new CoULD MHE Classification compared with existing systems (Masada, Gottschalk, Jo classifications); agreement measured by kappa coefficient
articles.take_home: Experts developed a new three-tier classification system for forearm changes in multiple hereditary exostoses that is more reliable than previous methods. The new system showed better agreement between different doctors assessing the same X-rays, making it more useful for monitoring how the condition develops over time.

articles.title: Youth With Eating Disorders Have a Higher 3-Month Rate of Adverse Postoperative Outcomes Following Common Orthopedic Surgeries.
articles.authors: Jha SA, Whitney DG, Stepanovich MT, Walick KS
articles.population: Young people aged 21 years and under undergoing spine surgery, arthroscopy or fracture surgery, with and without eating disorders
articles.sample_size: 1,057 young people with eating disorders and 170,582 without eating disorders
articles.outcomes: Procedure-related infection, wound complications, systemic complications, implant or hardware complications, and other procedure-related complications within 3 months of surgery
articles.take_home: Young people with eating disorders had significantly higher rates of complications after orthopaedic surgery within 3 months, including 88 per cent more overall complications and 129 per cent more infections than those without eating disorders. The risk of infection was particularly high in older teenagers aged 12 and above.

articles.title: Overcorrection Provides Better Final Coronal Plane Alignment in Genu Varum Patients Treated With Tension-Band Plating and Followed Up to Skeletal Maturity.
articles.authors: Sili MV, Aksoy T, Karademir OM, Kolac UC, Aksoy MC, Yilmaz G
articles.population: Skeletally immature patients with genu varum deformity treated with tension-band plating
articles.outcomes: Coronal plane alignment (mechanical lateral distal femoral angle and mechanical medial proximal tibial angle) measured preoperatively, at implant removal, and at final follow-up (median 88 months after implant removal)
articles.take_home: Children whose genu varum was intentionally overcorrected when the plate was removed were more likely to have normal leg alignment at final follow-up than those who were not overcorrected. The tibial side (shin bone) showed more tendency to shift back towards the original varus position after plate removal than the femoral side (thigh bone).

articles.title: Should we remove flexible intramedullary nails after diaphyseal forearm pediatric fracture? A cohort study of 288 patients.
articles.authors: Tirta M, Eikrem-Holsaeter A, Holt EB, Olsson R, Jakobsen RB, Randsborg PH
articles.population: Children with diaphyseal forearm fractures treated with flexible intramedullary nails
articles.sample_size: 288 patients (136 with implant removal, 152 with implant retention)
articles.outcomes: Primary: refracture rates and early refracture (before 12 months). Secondary: complications, infections, and healthcare resource use (outpatient visits and radiographic examinations)
articles.take_home: Keeping the flexible nails in place was well tolerated and did not increase refracture risk compared with removing them, and resulted in fewer hospital visits and imaging scans. The study was not large enough to detect small differences in refracture risk between the two approaches.

articles.title: Concordance and Discordance of Intraoperative Nerve Root Findings in Brachial Plexus Birth Injury.
articles.authors: Chen CJ, Zlotolow DA, Crowe CS, Park E, Kozin SH
articles.population: Infants with brachial plexus birth injury undergoing surgery
articles.outcomes: Agreement between preoperative injury classification and intraoperative nerve root findings; patterns of misclassification; influence of Horner syndrome
articles.take_home: Preoperative assessment of brachial plexus birth injury agreed with surgical findings in 83% of cases, but was particularly unreliable for identifying the full extent of injury involving the C8 nerve root. Horner syndrome may indicate more severe injury than initially suspected and should not be used alone to assess injury extent.
